title: A bit late is (probably) better than never!

posts.author: cuebitcrush
posts.body:
I've been here for a little bit now and neglected to introduce myself so why not do it now?
Hi there, I'm QB but I'm not particularly picky how you call me!
I'm an artist in general and I picked up pixel art so that I could make my own assets. Game dev is super new to me (as in "within the last month" new) and I've been starting off with RPG Maker 2003, but I've got a copy of MV as well so I'll likely get around to trying it out once I get the hang of RM software.
I'm yet unsure whether I'll post my current game here on account of it being my first one, but here's a drawing of the protagonist!
Nice to meet you!

posts.author: TESTOSTERONE

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome! Being an artist already gives you a jump start. Pretty much anyone can learn to do great things in RPG Maker if they are willing to invest the time and energy to learn how to use it. But not everyone has such an easy time with art.
Just a suggestion if you are brand new to RPG Maker. You might want to focus more on MV. It might not be a problem for you, but starting with RM2K3 and then switching to MV might be more confusing than just jumping in with MV.
If money isn't an issue, I would even suggest getting MZ instead, but that is a personal preference.
Anyway, good luck on your projects and if you are interested and willing, I would definitely post your current project. People post all sorts of projects that they are working on, even their very first projects.
Just remember to have fun!
